tool.name: Micrometer (calliper)
tool.measures: the dimensions of the stone: length, width, depth, in millimetres
tips: Measure the greatest length, then the width, then the height
Tighten gently: never force the stone
Write down the three numbers: they are used to estimate the weight

steps.title: Measuring without a balance
steps.text: The micrometer is a small precision calliper. It measures the stone to a tenth of a millimetre. You tighten it gently against the two sides of the stone and read the scale.

steps.title: Three measurements
Why measure?
steps.text: The dimensions describe the stone in a report, and above all they allow you to estimate the weight of a set stone, which cannot be put on the balance. Each cut and each material has its formula: the density of the stone comes into play. They also say whether the cut is well proportioned: a stone that is too deep or too flat loses its life.

steps.title: To remember
steps.text: • Length, width, depth, in millimetres. • Tighten without forcing, on the edges of the stone. • The dimensions are used to describe the stone and to estimate its weight when the balance is impossible.
